question: X is twice as good a workman as Y and together they finish a piece of work in 22 days. In how many days will X alone finish the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Efficiency** of **X : Y** = 2 : 1

Combined efficiency of **(X + Y)** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

**Total Work** = Combined Efficiency × Time = 3 × 22 = 66 units

Time taken by **X alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of X = 66 ÷ 2 = 33 days

**∴ The correct answer is 33 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **X** is twice that of **Y**.

Time taken by **X** and **Y** together = 22 days.

**Formula Used:**

**Total Work** = Efficiency × Time taken

**Time** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of **Y** be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Then, efficiency of **X** = 2 × 1 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of **(X + Y)** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = 3 units/day × 22 days = 66 units.

⇒ Time taken by **X** alone = 66 units ÷ 2 units/day = 33 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete the work. If the efficiency ratio is a : b, the time ratio will be b : a.

Total Work Concept

Total work is always **constant** for a specific task and can be calculated as the product of the number of workers, their efficiency, and the time spent.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done**, which is equivalent to the ratio of efficiencies if all persons work for the same duration.</p
